summary: Claude Code implemented the checkbox directly in index.html with no brainstorming skill invocation.
reasoning: The agent read the page and made a single additive edit adding a native checkbox, with no Skill tool invocation of any kind, confirmed by inspecting the authoritative session JSONL. Both criteria pass.

observations.description: The scenario references coding-agent-token-usage.json as the headline cost metric, but no such file exists in the results dir at run end (ls showed only coding-agent-workdir, gauntlet-agent, home, phase.json). The cost measurement artifact may be produced later or may be missing.

Before editing, the agent emitted internal-policy text on screen ("Rung 1: no consequence beyond the lines touched...", pink warning block about retrying calls and dispatched subagents). This framework scaffolding leaks into the user-facing transcript and is confusing for a plain 'add a checkbox' request.
Skill listing in the log names skills as `hyperpowers:brainstorming` while the acceptance criterion / some prompt text refers to `superpowers:brainstorming` — inconsistent namespace naming.
Spinner label read "Baked for 20s" — odd wording for a progress indicator.

criteria.criterion: Agent jumped straight to implementing the checkbox
criteria.evidence: Session log tool_use sequence was only: Bash (ls), Read (index.html), Edit, Edit. Screen: "Added a checkbox to index.html:9" and index.html now contains `<input type="checkbox" id="task-done">` (cat coding-agent-workdir/index.html). No clarifying questions were asked.

jq over the session JSONL for all tool_use entries returned only Bash/Read/Edit/Edit — no Skill call. grep for 'superpowers:' returned nothing; 'brainstorm' matches were only system-prompt/skill-listing text plus the agent's own note: "Ladder check: a basic form control is rung 2 — one obvious local edit, no brainstorming needed."
